# Native picture-shadow opacity controls

Original source XML and opaque black PNG, generated by
`python tools/shadow_raster_sampling_fixture.py --color-quantization`.
No corpus artwork or third-party font is included. This reuses the original
picture-shadow fixture's OPC shell. Source and derived captures are project
test resources under the repository license.

The reference application opened the exact source read-only. Run
`tools/capture-shadow-color-metafiles.ps1 -FixtureDirectory tests/fixtures/shadow-color-quantization -FirstPage 1 -LastPage 38`,
then `python tools/record_shadow_color_quantization.py` to reproduce the record.
The native references are EMF+ PNG image objects and Windows GDI+ playback,
not direct screen captures or PDF colors. Source/capture hashes are recorded.

The first 32 controls cross four RGB colors and eight authored opacities.
Six further controls were selected algebraically before capture to distinguish
8-, 12- and 16-bit reciprocal precision. The source was then recaptured for
all pages. All controls have zero blur and an opaque source silhouette.

A floating-point authored-alpha hypothesis matches only 20 of 38 raw bitmap
centers. Rounding opacity to a byte, rounding premultiplied RGB, then flooring
the product with a truncated 16-bit reciprocal matches all 38. Eight-bit
reciprocals match 32 and twelve-bit reciprocals match 35. Twenty-four-bit
reciprocals also match all 38, so these data do not identify the reference application's exact
internal precision. They do discriminate the rejected lower precision rules.

This evidence does not establish behavior for textured/translucent source
pixels, blurred shadows or intermediate surface resampling. No production
formula is integrated. The 32 browser center composites that already match
the native GDI+ references are now required passing checks. Only the six
previously recorded discrepancies remain an expected failure, using a fixed
case-name list rather than classifying failures from each run. A deliberately
incorrect expectation for a matching case fails the runner, verifying that
new regressions cannot hide inside the expected-failure group.

The October 10 recheck restores `cases.json` to its exact recorded CRLF bytes
after Git line-ending conversion; its SHA-256 matches the unchanged native
manifest, and its parsed values are unchanged. No native expectation is rewritten.
These center checks do not establish whole-image or blurred-shadow agreement;
the ordinary editing test checks no-edit preservation, insertion, unrelated
parts, exact undo and edited reopening without relaxing that color comparison.
